title: Closure checks that do not dispatch, named rather than tolerated
note: contracts/custody.schema.json calls a closure check 'a closure condition somebody can run' and validates only that the expression is a non-empty string. scripts/sov_closure_checks.py reads the string and drives each declared command as far as its argument parser. The entries below fail that reading and were already failing before it existed. Their provenance is worth stating exactly, because an earlier draft of this note got it wrong: these are not commands broken by a CLI redesign. `git log -S` over the whole history finds no commit in which conformance/run.py took --scenario, sov_ainative.py took --check, sov_capability.py declared an enforcement subcommand, sov_node.py declared admit, or the Record Service CLI declared verify. Every one of these expressions was authored aspirationally and never ran, so there is no earlier form for a repair to restore. They are recorded as debt rather than a refusal on the attribution principle scripts/sov_phase_progress.py uses for the phase floor: a fall is attributable to the edit that caused it and refuses, and none of these is attributable to the concern that found them. None gates the active phase - six carry the closed phase:i and one carries no phase. Widening this list is the tolerance CLAUDE.md refuses, and three guards hold the entrance and the exit: an entry that starts dispatching fails, an entry naming a custody no collection declares fails, and an entry with no observed error, no reason, or no repair seat fails. Deleting an entry is the repair.

refuses.CLOSURE_CHECK_DEBT_REPAIRED: an entry here now dispatches, so the entry is stale and must be deleted rather than left as cover for the next one
refuses.CLOSURE_CHECK_DEBT_UNKNOWN: an entry here names a custody or expression that no collection declares
refuses.CLOSURE_CHECK_DEBT_UNATTRIBUTED: an entry here carries no observed failure and no seat that can repair it

debt.reason: conformance/run.py takes --cases and --observations and has never taken --scenario at any commit; the oracle grades the whole corpus in one reading and has always done so. The expression describes a per-scenario selection the oracle never offered.
debt.repair: decide whether binding parity closes on the whole-corpus reading (python conformance/run.py) or whether the oracle should regain per-scenario selection; both are reachable and the choice is the custody holder's, not this reader's.

debt.reason: the same expression as custody:phase-i/binding-parity, carried by a second custody; one repair settles both.

debt.observed: sov_ainative.py: error: argument command: invalid choice: '3' (choose from 'grade', 'scenarios', 'selfcheck')
debt.reason: sov_ainative.py has never had a --check flag; its history begins with the grade, scenarios and selfcheck subcommands it has now. Which of them grades AI-NATIVE check 3 is a reading of AI-NATIVE.md, not a rename.
debt.repair: name the subcommand and argument that grade AI-NATIVE check 3, then replace the expression.

debt.observed: sov_capability: error: argument command: invalid choice: 'enforcement' (choose from 'events', 'build', 'check', 'show', 'offices')
debt.reason: sov_capability.py has never declared an enforcement subcommand; it declares events, build, check, show and offices. 'events' judges emitted receipt events against the map and is the nearest reading, but whether that is what authority enforcement closes on is the custody holder's judgement.
debt.repair: decide whether 'events' or 'check' is the closure reading for authority enforcement, then replace the expression.

debt.observed: sov_node: error: argument command: invalid choice: 'admit' (choose from 'status', 'peers', 'validate')
debt.reason: sov_node.py has never declared an admit subcommand, and the expression names an admission, which is an act rather than a reading. A closure check that performed an admission would settle the thing it grades.
debt.repair: replace with the reading that shows a session was admitted as a node - 'validate' or 'peers' - rather than the act of admitting one.

debt.observed: Error while finding module specification for 'soveraeign_record_service.cli' (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'soveraeign_record_service')
debt.reason: Two faults, not one. The package lives at services/record/src/ and is not on the path from the repository root, so the import fails first and hides the second: with PYTHONPATH set, the CLI answers 'invalid choice: verify' - it declares verify-export and restore-journal, and has never declared verify. Recording the PYTHONPATH form alone moves this entry from UNIMPORTABLE to REJECTED and does not clear it.
debt.repair: name the subcommand that verifies the journal - verify-export is the nearest declared one - and make the package reachable from the root, either by recording the PYTHONPATH form in the expression or by giving the Record Service a console entry point.
